guide.metaDescription: Run your business on Abonten as a team: make a team, invite people, give each one a role and work as the team.
guide.title: Run your business on Abonten as a team
guide.lede: One account for the business, with its own name, @username, events, money and messages. Everyone on your team signs in with their own Abonten account and gets a role that covers only what they need. Nobody shares a password.
guide.teamAccountBody: The team account: its own @username, events, places, followers, money and inbox.
guide.fitsNote: Customers only ever see the business. Inside the team, every action is recorded with the name of the person who took it, and every Owner can see that activity.
guide.step1Body: The person who will run the business on Abonten opens <path>Settings › Teams › Make a team</path> on the website or in the app.
guide.step1Point1: Give the team its name and an @username (letters, numbers and underscores).
guide.step1Point2: Confirm you're 18 or older: teams on Abonten are run by adults.
guide.step1Point3: You become the team's first Owner.
guide.step1Tip: Already selling events on your own account? Choose Make your organizer account a team instead. Your events, followers and organizer money move to the team, and you get a new @username for yourself.
guide.step2Body: An Owner opens the team and taps <path>Invite</path>.
guide.step2Point1: Invite by their @username or by phone number.
guide.step2Point2: Pick the role that covers only what they need (see the roles below).
guide.step2Point3: The invitation stays open for a week. A number with no Abonten account yet gets a text: they sign up with that number to accept.
guide.step3Body: Each person sees the invitation in their notifications and under Settings › Teams › Invitations, and taps Accept.
guide.step3Point2: Their own tickets, credit and private messages stay theirs.
guide.step4Body: Choose the team under Managing as: in Manage on the website, or at the top of Organizer in the app. Switch back to your own account the same way.
guide.step4Point1: What you see then depends on your role: Door staff only check people in, Finance sees the money, and so on.
guide.step4Point2: Publish events while managing as the team, so they belong to the business and not to you.
guide.sketchEventsBody: Ticket types, dates, promo codes, attendee list, check-in
guide.exampleTitle: A line-up for a theatre run
guide.exampleOwner: Whoever runs the company on Abonten (one or two people)
guide.exampleFinance: The person who handles ticket money and payouts
guide.exampleManager: The person who sets up shows, dates and ticket types
guide.exampleContent: The person who answers customers and posts videos
guide.exampleDoor: Ushers scanning tickets on show nights
guide.note1: Only Owners and Finance can ask for the team's payouts, and only Owners can change where the money goes. Changing the payout account needs a recent sign-in, every Owner is told, and the first payout to a new account waits 48 hours.
guide.note2: Members can leave at any time. The last Owner names another Owner first. Owners can remove members, and their access ends at once.
guide.note3: Your own team members don't earn promoter commission on your events unless an Owner adds them as a promoter of that event.
guide.note4: Team accounts are opening to businesses one by one. Abonten switches them on for your business before you start.
guide.readHelp: Read the help page on team accounts
guide.roleBody: {role, select, owner {Everything: members and roles, the team's profile, payout account and payouts, refunds, events, places, check-in, messages and verification. A team always has at least one Owner.} finance {Earnings, payouts, refunds and money reports, and featuring the team's events.} manager {Events, the place page, ticket types, promo codes, bookings, the attendee list and check-in.} content {Customer messages, Spotlight videos and Stories, and replies to reviews.} door {Scanning tickets at the door, nothing else. They never see who is coming.} front_desk {Booking requests and the place's visit QR code. Owners can limit them to some of the team's places.} other {}}

profileBody: This is what people see on the team's page. Only Owners can change it.
socialHint: Abonten names these accounts when it shares the team's events.
usernameMoveNote: Links to the old username keep working for 30 days, and nobody else can take it in that time.
deleteIntro: Deleting the team takes its page off Abonten and removes everyone from it. Every Owner has to agree.
deleteEffectMembers: Everyone is removed from the team and open invitations are withdrawn. Their own accounts aren't affected.
deleteEffectListings: Upcoming events nobody holds tickets for are cancelled and the rest are archived. The team's places stay on Abonten without an owner, so they can be claimed again.
deleteEffectProfile: The team's page, photo, followers, alerts and Spotlight posts go. Its conversations close.
deleteEffectMoney: Sales and payout records are kept as a financial record. Any Abonten credit the team has is lost.
deleteEffectOwners: {others, plural, =0 {You're the only Owner, so the team is deleted as soon as you confirm.} one {The other Owner has 7 days to approve, or the request ends.} other {The other # Owners have 7 days to approve, or the request ends.}}
deleteSignInNote: For your security, this works only if you signed in within the last 15 minutes.
deletePendingTitleNoActor: An Owner asked to delete this team
deleteWaiting: {owners, plural, one {Waiting for {waiting} of # Owner} other {Waiting for {waiting} of # Owners}}
deleteEndsOn: The request ends on {date} if not every Owner has approved.
deleteApproveBody: Once every Owner approves, the team is deleted. This can't be undone.
deleteYouApproved: You approved. The team is deleted once every Owner approves.
deleteStopBody: The team stays as it is, and the other Owners are told.
